subject: Clarifying capture horizon for requests, prompts, and generated outputs
messages:
From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@brightbank.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-21T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Questions on default capture window for requests/outputs

Hi Tessa,

Thanks for the demo today — BrightBank security had a few follow-ups around default data capture and retention. Can you confirm the following in writing so we can close our triangle with legal?

1) By default, how long do you retain raw request/response logs (including full prompts and model outputs) for hosted accounts?
2) Are prompts treated differently from model-generated outputs for retention or deletion requests?
3) How do streaming sessions (partial tokens sent during an open stream) get captured and later purged?
4) Do derivatives (embeddings, reranks, transcripts) derived from customer data follow the same deletion path as the original request?
5) If we ask for account-wide purge, what is the expected timeline (including backups and tombstones)?

I've attached our questionnaire (BrightBank_Security_Questions.xlsx) with the items marked we care most about. Appreciated if you can loop in product/security.

Thanks,
Jordan
Jordan Lee
Security Engineer — BrightBank
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@brightbank.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-21T17:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on default capture window for requests/outputs

Jordan —

Appreciate the clear list. Below is a concise summary of Redwood's default behavior for hosted accounts; I’ve included operational details you can hand to legal. Marissa and Karthik are cc'd for any product nuance.

- Default retention windows (hosted):
  * Request/response logs (request payloads and associated raw model outputs): 30 days by default.
  * Prompt texts submitted via API: captured as part of request logs and subject to the same 30-day window.
  * Model-generated outputs that are material derivatives (saved artifacts like transcripts and reranks): 90 days by default unless explicitly configured by the customer.

- Prompts vs outputs:
  * Prompts are treated as request metadata — retained under the request log window (30 days).
  * Outputs that are persisted to object storage (e.g., exported transcripts, stored summaries, embeddings created via the embeddings endpoint) are treated as customer artifacts and follow the longer artifact retention window (90 days) unless the customer opts into a different policy or dedicated/private deployment.

- Streaming sessions: partial tokens emitted during an open streaming connection are buffered by the runtime for delivery and are not persisted beyond the standard request log unless the application explicitly sets a flag to persist intermediate transcripts. If persisted, they follow the artifact retention window.

- Derivatives and deletion:
  * When a customer requests deletion, we remove both the raw request/response entries and any directly associated derivatives that Redwood controls (embeddings created by the platform, reranks stored in our artifact store) within the purge workflow.
  * Third-party integrations where customers export or copy artifacts (S3 exports, external analytics) are not automatically removed by Redwood — we provide APIs and guidance for customers to perform deletions in those external systems.

- Purge timeline and backups:
  * Account-wide purge request submitted via support or the Data Delete API: initial removal from primary indexes and customer-facing stores within 48 hours.
  * Tombstone process and background purge jobs remove accessible artifacts within 7 days.
  * Backups and cold snapshots: best-effort purge from backups within 90 days; customers requiring shorter backup windows can negotiate Dedicated/Private configurations or contractual SLAs.

I’m attaching a short one-pager with these bullets. If this level of detail works, I’ll send an entry-level description for legal and a separate, more technical annex for your infra/security team.

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-21T19:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on default capture window for requests/outputs

Quick internal note before we send to Jordan: a couple of product/legal clarifications we should include in the customer-facing text:

- Make explicit that "prompts" captured by web SDKs (when the web SDK opt-in is enabled) have the same retention as API requests.
- Call out that embeddings are considered "derivatives" and that our deletion flow updates the vector index to remove vectors referencing deleted requests; however, depending on the index provider, vector rebuilds may take up to 72 hours.
- For streaming persistence, add the exact flag name "persist_streaming_transcript" that customers would set.

Kimberly, can you add a line on legal hold behavior (court order/preserve-request)? I want to avoid implying immediate removal where legal constraints apply.

-M
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@brightbank.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-22T08:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on default capture window for requests/outputs

Jordan —

Following up with the finalized language (attached). Key items that precise legal teams typically want are below. I’ve kept the wording short for your legal counsel; the annex we can share with your infra/security folks.

1) Default retention: request logs & prompts retained 30 days; persisted artifacts/derivatives retained 90 days. Customers can shorten both windows with Dedicated/Private setups or contracts.

2) Streaming: we do not persist interim tokens unless "persist_streaming_transcript" is enabled. If enabled, those transcripts are governed as persisted artifacts.

3) Deletion path:
   - Submit Data Delete request via console or Data Delete API.
   - Primary store removal begins within 48 hours.
   - Tombstone/secondary purge completes within 7 days.
   - Backups: best-effort removal within 90 days; customers can request a backup sweep via support for high-priority purges.

4) Derivatives: Redwood-managed derivatives (embeddings, stored reranks, transcripts persisted in our artifact store) are included in the Redwood deletion workflow. External exports are out of scope; we provide logs and APIs to help customers find and delete copies.

5) Legal hold: if BrightBank has a preservation requirement (subpoena, litigation hold), please notify us; legal holds will prevent automatic deletion workflows for the scope identified and are handled by our legal and compliance teams.

Attachments: redwood-retention-one-pager.pdf (customer-friendly) and the technical annex link in the drive for your infra team.

If you want, Kimberly can draft a short statement for formal sign-off that references our SOC2 and retention appendix.

Best,
Tessa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
